correctness.rationale: Final assessment of /workspace/repairs/3/RESULT.md. The original mathematical inequalities and counts are valid; the corrected claim centers the distinct support classification and fixes the comparison with earlier work. Independent proof: the local masks at each prime are exactly the neighboring classes -a-1 and -a; CRT justifies independent phases and provides some good start. Without prime 3, the single-mask maxima for 5,7,11,13,large are 6,4,4,3,2, so only 5,7,11 could cover fourteen, and their masks would need to be disjoint and maximal. Every size-four mask for 11 hits both 1 and 2 modulo 5; every size-six mask for 5 hits at least one of those classes. Thus 3 is necessary. The uncovered progression modulo 3 has four or five entries and the other primes have at most two each, hence there must be exactly four entries (2,5,8,11), forcing a=2 mod 3. Prime 11 or larger can hit at most one of these, as differences 3,6,9 cannot be 0 or ±1 modulo such a prime. This forces 5,7. In the four consecutive q coordinates with i=3q-1, prime 7 must take {1,3} or {2,4}, and prime 5 takes the complement. The two phase choices give the CRT solutions a=2 and 89 modulo 105. A fifteen-run would have two consecutive fourteen-run starts, impossible for these two phases. Lifting to prime powers gives 2N/105 starts modulo N. This elementary check is given in full in the corrected file. I also independently enumerated exact set masks generated by (i+s)(i+s+1)=0 modulo each small prime and empty, singleton, and neighboring-pair masks for the large class. All 26 original table entries matched; only (3,5,7) has complete unions, two in number. A cyclic scan of the 105 good-start gaps gave exactly (start,length)=(2,14),(89,14) at length >=14. VERIFICATION.md and verify_paired_sieve_14.py were inspected without executing the supplied code. The proof and alternate finite certificate apply to exactly three distinct odd primes regardless of multiplicity, not to even moduli or all offsets.

evidence: The original function maximizes the bad length over offsets; j2(N)-1 is the run length. Lemmas 1.1 and 1.2 give j2(2M)=2j2(M) for odd M and j2(3M)=3j2(M) when 3 does not divide M. The computational note tabulates primorials only, and ancillary §3.4 says its algorithms may be applied to arbitrary prime sets, not that such a classification was computed.
broader_coverage.reasoning: These results directly bound the fixed-offset quantity by j2(N)-1 and imply the fourteen bound for every support containing 3: each of the other primes >=5 covers at most two of five indices. This is broader upper-bound coverage, not classification of when the bound can be met at a single prescribed offset. A theorem for primorial supports and a general algorithm do not settle the extremal support among all distinct triples.

evidence: To fill fourteen at 105 the 3-mask must leave only four positions, namely i=3q-1 for q=1,...,4. The residue pair at remaining prime p is {-a/3,(1-a)/3}, with difference ±3^(-1), i.e. ±2 for p=5,7. Filtering the six prior rows leaves exactly rows 2 and 5; CRT with a=2 mod 3 gives 2 and 89. For supports with 3 but a prime >=11, the same fixed-offset condition prohibits two hits in those four positions; no general arbitrary-offset result provides that prohibition.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Therefore the earlier primorial data mechanically give the entire 105 subcase, including the two starts, once converted to offset one. The distinct exclusion of all other supports requires fixed adjacency: large primes cannot supply two hits at distances 3,6,9 after peeling 3, and supports without 3 require the disjointness obstruction for 5 and 11. The earlier paired function allows offsets with other local differences and so does not by its value distinguish such equality cases. The full reach of Nguyen's potentially equivalent reformulation is unverified.

evidence: For odd N, replacing offset one by either N+1 or 1-N gives the same residue tests at an even signed offset. Ziller–Morack explicitly exploit parity adjustment over odd-prime wheels in Lemma 1.4. The Resultary exact hit 90cf4b3dd6c6 is the frozen record itself. The distinct 29d844172410 Finding is about input-translated X^2+1 and has a seven-run bound and different extremizers. Kalmynin–Konyagin translate polynomial outputs, x+f(i). The accessible description of Nguyen concerns symmetric pairs about a fixed center; full text could not be compared.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Offset one is genuinely a restriction of the paired Jacobsthal setting, not outside it by parity. Also gcd tests for (C-q,C+q) are identical for (q-C,q+C) by negation, and 2C can equal one modulo odd N; a fixed-center symmetric pair result could therefore overlap, depending on windows and quantifiers. Input translation of X(X+1) changes its linear coefficient as a varies; output translation of a fixed polynomial cannot reproduce that family by changing only x. X^2+1 has different local roots (e.g. none at 3), so the same-day quadratic result does not give this classification.

originality.rationale: PASS for the corrected contribution: among every odd three-prime support, only 3,5,7 can attain fourteen for offset one. The frozen comparison understated prior coverage: Ziller–Morack's published primorial table plus ancillary lemmas imply the fourteen bound at 105 and at every support containing 3, and the ancillary exact residue table gives both starts at 105 by a direct filter. The replacement credits these mechanical implications rather than claiming originality for those facts in isolation. The earlier data and broader uniform-offset lemmas do not exclude fourteen at other supports for the fixed adjacent offset; the repaired proof supplies this exclusion. The symmetric-pair overlap is a genuine residual risk, not a parity distinction or an originality verdict by itself.
residual_risks: Nguyen's full text could not be inspected and its centered-pair setup is mathematically relevant. There may be an unindexed equivalent all-support fixed-offset classification. Prior coverage of the primorial subcase and the broader upper bound on supports with 3 is verified, not treated as residual.

value.rationale: The useful fact is rigidity for a fixed adjacent pair: maximizing over offsets loses which supports can actually attain the obstruction at lag one. The theorem identifies exactly the one exceptional wheel among infinitely many supports and explains its rigidity through the surviving step-three progression and the separate disjointness obstruction when 3 is absent. This gives an actionable exclusion for all other odd three-prime supports; value does not rest on recomputing the known smallest-wheel example or its two phases.
